observations.observation: The earliest traceable public report located was Bloomberg’s Sep. 24, 8:25 a.m. EDT (12:25Z) story: unnamed sources said Oracle had sent a force-majeure notice to the Jupiter developer and sought possible payment deferral if the campus missed its 2028 target, rather than leaving as tenant. The report does not specify when the notice was sent.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: This is source-based reporting, not the notice itself; the underlying notice, exact transmission time, and operative contract terms were not public in the reviewed sources.

observations.observation: Bloomberg’s page shows a 12:50 p.m. EDT update (16:50Z), before cutoff. The update describes any rent delay as conditional on agreement that a power-related force-majeure event occurred; it says other interim costs remain due, rent remains owed over the lease term, and the notice is not a financing default.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The article says the legal effect was uncertain and relies on unnamed sources for contractual mechanics; no public notice or lease language was located.

observations.observation: Before the notice report, Oracle had announced a Jupiter design using up to 2.45 GW of Bloom fuel cells and said construction was on schedule. By Aug. 18, public reporting from FERC filings said the Green Chile gas pipeline’s expected service date had shifted from August 2026 to February 2027; Oracle nevertheless said Jupiter remained on schedule.
observations.event_time: 2026-08-13 (FERC filing accession; the media report attributes the date change to recent filings)
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The pipeline delay was a known supply-side issue, but the cited public material did not itself report a change to the campus schedule or a change to Bloom’s project scope.

observations.observation: Oracle’s Sep. 14 statement distinguished the campus construction from the separate proposed microgrid and its air-permit review. On Sep. 17, the New Mexico Supreme Court denied emergency challenges and lifted stays, allowing proceedings to resume; this was not an air-permit approval.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The pending air-permit process remained unresolved; the Sep. 17 court action removed interim stays but did not decide the permit’s merits.

observations.observation: Same-day reporting relayed Oracle’s position that Jupiter remained on schedule and that force-majeure notices do not by themselves change delivery expectations; Blue Owl said the notice did not change the project’s financial commitments. The Information and TechCrunch identified Bloomberg as the first report.
observations.event_time: 2026-09-24 (company responses; exact response time not stated)
observations.publication_time: 2026-09-24T18:11:00Z (TechCrunch; The Information published at 7:48 a.m. PDT)
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: These outlets relay statements and Bloomberg reporting; neither provides the notice or a public contract record, and no Bloom-specific response or project-level change was established.

gaps: No public copy of the notice or lease provisions was located; exact service/receipt time, force-majeure trigger, payment scope, and whether the parties agreed to the asserted terms remain unknown.
The supplied W1 refers to an earlier rumor, but it does not include a public source URL or publication time, and this focused search did not locate an independently timestamped pre-Bloomberg rumor.
No reviewed pre-cutoff source establishes that the notice changed Bloom’s order, capacity, shipment, project schedule, or revenue terms. No Bloom-specific response was located.
The Bloomberg updated page is timestamped before cutoff, but the reported legal mechanics remain source-attributed and were not independently checked against a public contract.
research_notes: Scope: sources available by the 2026-09-24T20:50:27.782652Z cutoff only. The earliest traceable public report located is Bloomberg’s Sep. 24, 8:25 a.m. EDT story, syndicated by Yahoo Finance. It reports that Oracle had sent a force-majeure notice, citing people familiar with the matter; the notice’s actual send time is not stated, and no notice or contract text was located. Bloomberg’s page displays a 12:50 p.m. EDT update, also before cutoff. The Information and TechCrunch subsequently identify Bloomberg as the first report, so their repetition is dissemination, not independent confirmation. Prior public context included Oracle’s announced Bloom fuel-cell design and on-schedule statements, alongside a reported Green Chile pipeline delay. The Sep. 17 court action lifted interim stays but did not itself issue the pending air permit. Oracle and Blue Owl’s same-day statements counter the inference that the notice itself changed the project schedule or financial commitments. The supplied W1 refers to an earlier rumor, but no independently dated public source for that rumor was identified; it is not possible to establish its publication time from the supplied material.
